Coram:
Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C') has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 593/2019, registered at Police Station Bhalswa Dairy, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. R.P.S.
Bhatti and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Sohan Lal from Police Station Bhalswa Dairy, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 had been solemnized on 07.12.2015.
No child was born out of this wedlock.
It is stated that due to misunderstanding and temperamental differences, the complainant/respondent no. 2 left the company of the petitioner and started living separately since 26.01.2015.

On the complaint of complainant/respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 593/2019 was registered at Police Station Bhalswa Dairy, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC against petitioners.

It is further stated that petitioners and respondent no. 2 have resolved their disputes amicably before Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi vide Settlement Agreement Subhash Chandra & Ors vs The State(Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93269161/
1 dated 24.11.2021.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between them and they have obtained decree of divorce by mutual consent from the concerned Court.

6. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

7. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 3,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in first motion.
b. Second instalment of Rs.1,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in second motion.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs.50,000/- to be paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR before Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
8.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 50,000/- today, i.e., 23.03.2023 vide DD No. 468235 drawn on Indian Bank,
Mayur Vihar, Delhi, and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 593/2019, registered at Police Station Bhalswa Dairy, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 23, 2023/
